title: The autopsy
lede: Tap a cause to see the evidence. The percentages are our editorial weighting. The evidence under each one is sourced.

causes.title: It lost the format war to Best Buy
causes.text: Best Buy’s self-service stores with central checkouts and low-margin traffic builders passed the Circuit City stores in revenue by fiscal 1996 and reached $40.0B by fiscal 2008, against $11.7B.[^24][^7][^1] Alan Wurtzel said the company “systematically positioned ourselves for the older market and excluded the younger generation.”[^32]

causes.title: It dismantled its own sales floor
causes.text: Commissions ended in February 2003, with 3,900 dismissals according to the Richmond Fed. In March 2007 another 3,400 employees were let go for being paid above the market range.[^3][^29][^10] The company itself listed the effect on morale and reputation as a risk.[^1]

causes.title: Suppliers and lenders pulled back in 2008
causes.text: Vendors cut credit lines and some demanded payment before shipment. A new inventory appraisal reduced what the company could borrow. The disclosure statement names three causes of the filing: “erosion of vendor confidence,” “decreased liquidity” and “a global economic crisis.”[^13][^17]

causes.title: The cash had been handed back
causes.text: Buyback authorisations rose from $200M in 2003 to $1.2B in 2006, and $966.3M of that had been used by March 2008 (derived).[^1] The Richmond Fed puts the average price near $20 a share. Wurtzel: when the recession came, “the cupboard was bare.”[^29][^31]

causes.title: Distractions and reversals
causes.text: Divx cost $219.3M after tax (derived).[^6] The 2000 exit from appliances removed 14% of sales just before a housing boom.[^5][^29] InterTAN, bought for $259.3M in 2004, brought a $92M goodwill write-down within three years.[^9][^10]

disclaimer: the weights are an interpretive model by the Spectre Brands editors, not a measured quantity. The filings document the symptoms. How much each one contributed is a matter of opinion.
